policy_note: Allowlist for the EcoGuard server dependency audit gate (scripts/dependency-audit.js). Entries track HIGH/CRITICAL findings in the PRODUCTION tree that have NO non-major fix — i.e. they are blocked by an upstream package. Every entry MUST carry a reason and an expiry date; when an entry expires the CI gate fails until the situation is re-reviewed. Never add an entry for something `npm audit fix` (without --force) could resolve in-range. LOW/MODERATE findings are not allowlisted: they are reported as non-blocking warnings.
root_cause: All five entries below are one cluster. sqlite3@5.1.7 (a direct production dependency) ships its install-time toolchain as regular/optional dependencies: tar@^6.1.11 (prebuilt-binary extraction via prebuild-install) and node-gyp@8.x (source-compile fallback). node-gyp pulls make-fetch-happen -> cacache -> tar@6.x. The only true leaf advisory is node-tar (12 GHSAs, marked critical); every 'high' record above it (cacache, make-fetch-happen, node-gyp, sqlite3) is npm audit bubbling the tar cluster up the chain to the direct dependency. Every patched node-tar release is 7.x, so sqlite3@5's declared tar@^6.1.11 range caps the tree at tar 6.2.1. npm reports the sole fix as sqlite3@6.0.1 (isSemVerMajor: true). These CVEs are exploitable only while npm unpacks archives during 'npm install' — the running server never invokes tar or node-gyp. Fix: upgrade sqlite3 to 6.x (major upgrade, deliberately deferred).

entries.reason: Aggregator record: the sqlite3 driver itself has no advisory; npm flags it high because its install toolchain (node-gyp/tar, see root_cause) is unfixable below sqlite3@6.0.1 (major). Runtime DB access via the driver is unaffected by these install-time CVEs. Review for the sqlite3@6 upgrade at expiry.

Optional dependency of sqlite3@5.1.7; only executed when npm compiles sqlite3 from source as a fallback (never by the running service). Patched toolchain versions are only reachable via sqlite3@6 (major).
node-gyp dependency used to download source/headers during install. Build-time only; fixed in sqlite3@6's toolchain.
make-fetch-happen dependency; npm cache layer of the node-gyp install chain. Build-time only; its finding is the transitive tar advisory.

The single true leaf CVE cluster (node-tar: path traversal, symlink/hardlink escape, decompression DoS). Installed 6.2.1, used ONLY to unpack sqlite3 prebuilt binaries at install time (prebuild-install + node-gyp); never invoked at runtime. All patched releases are tar 7.x, blocked by sqlite3@5.1.7's tar@^6.1.11 range. New tar advisories beyond the listed 12 GHSAs will fail CI.
